title: Tomorrow Can Worry About Itself
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Beginning with a personal anecdote about a daughter overwhelmed at bedtime by the week’s demands, Stuart draws a direct parallel to the professional overwhelm teachers face from the ever-present gap between what could be done and what has been done. He anchors the piece in two ancient sources—Robert Louis Stevenson’s ‘anyone can carry their burden until nightfall’ and the Sermon on the Mount’s ‘tomorrow will worry about itself’—as expressions of the same insight: human beings are finite, and the antidote to anxious overwhelm is containment within the present day’s scope. The article draws autobiographical weight from Stuart’s own third-year burnout and subsequent year in service jobs in New York City, where shift-bounded work helped him relearn how to leave the job at the end of the day. The concept of satisficing emerges as the classroom application: doing something well enough, rather than perfectly, and trusting Tomorrow You to handle what remains.
points: Human beings are finite, time-bound creatures—worrying about tomorrow does not move tasks forward, it simply drains today’s finite energy without producing any of tomorrow’s results.
Robert Louis Stevenson’s ‘anyone can carry his burden, however hard, until nightfall’ reframes finitude as a feature rather than a limitation: the scope is manageable if the unit is one day.

Stuart’s own three-year burnout and subsequent year in service jobs taught him what no PD could: shift-bounded work that cannot follow you home trains the habit of leaving, and that habit is transferable to teaching.

The concept of satisficing—doing something well enough rather than perfectly—is named as the classroom application of the ‘tomorrow will worry about itself’ principle, giving teachers a decision rule for when to stop.
The article is addressed as much to teacher wellbeing as to classroom practice, positioning present-day containment as a professional sustainability strategy rather than a motivational platitude.
quotes: Anyone can carry his burden, however hard, until nightfall. Anyone can do his work, however hard, for one day. Anyone can live sweetly, patiently, lovingly, purely, till the sun goes down. And this is all life really means.

the central truth is an important source of strength for both my daughter and me when we get overwhelmed: human beings are finite, time-bound creatures. We CAN worry about tomorrow, but it doesn’t DO anything.

In teaching, one of the ideas you’ve got to make peace with is that there is always more you could do. It took me my first three years of teaching, working 70+ hour workweeks, grinding myself into dust, to come to this conclusion.

In each of those three jobs, I couldn’t work at home. It was just: show up to the shift, do the things the job required, and steadily practice the knowledge and skills of the job until my capabilities increased.
It did help me go to sleep at night. It helped me learn how to let work be a work thing and life outside of work be a life-outside-of-work thing.
